Could AI help solve a 167-year-old puzzle?

Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859. It concerns the distribution of prime numbers.

Alpöge shared a four-page summary and more than 175,000 Lean files for computer verification. He says Claude helped throughout the research, accelerating progress near the end.

The hypothesis is one of seven Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, each worth $1 million. No independent experts have verified the proof yet. Initial checks confirmed the files match and key statements compile; full verification is underway. A prize requires journal publication and two years of broad acceptance.
